messages.author: f0732d7bffc290cf
messages.subject: zero-encounter surveys
parts:
Hi All,
I am currently using DISTANCE 5 to analyse some bird survey data from
rainforest in Northern Australia. At the moment I am concentrating on
estimating total abundance for a species which is largely restricted to
upland forests. My data are distances to birds from survey transects in
forests at different altitudes (for which I have estimates of total
areas of forest) My question is: When using DISTANCE to estimate their
total abundance in each stratum, I ought to include those surveys at
lower altitudes where the birds are at lower abundance, including those
surveys that failed to detect any. if I include these as simply surveys
with blanks where perp_distance should be, is this achieved? If so, I
would like some help understanding how DISTANCE incorporates these zero
encounter surveys into its estimates of D and N...
Any help would be much appreciated.
Cheers

Alex Anderson

Phd Candidate,
Centre for Tropical Biodiversity and Climate Change
School of Marine and Tropical Biology
James Cook University
Townsville, Queensland, 4811
email: alexander...@jcu.edu.au

messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: zero-encounter surveys
parts:
Alex:

I'm not certain I am using terms exactly as you do. But I interpret
your term 'surveys' as 'transects.' From that starting point, you
*must* include information about sampling effort you exerted (even if it
did not result in detections) in your analysis. Very roughly stated,
the estimate of density of birds (simplifying to say all detections are
of groups of size 1) follows this formula (Eqn 2.11, p38 of Buckland et
al (2001)):
density = [f(0)/2] x [n/L]

The first bit encompasses the estimation of the detection function. It
is the second bit that is defined as the 'encounter rate' (number of
detections per amount of effort exerted; for line transects this is
measured in length of line travelled). If you provide lengths only for
transects on which birds are detected, you'll overestimate this
encounter rate, and hence overestimate density.

Therefore, you must include transects (and their length) with no
detections. If you look at the 'Stratify example.dst' in the Sample
Projects directory, you'll see that no objects were detected on
transects labelled 5, 6, 9, 10, 11,12, and 23. That is how your project
ought to look.
